chapters.title: An upload needs an allowance
chapters.lead:
<rr-mermaid class="rr-diagram-delta">flowchart TD
 A[Account] --> H[Handler, changed]:::changed
 H --> S[Store]
 click A "rr:code/internal/upload/account.go"
 click H "rr:sym/ServeHTTP"
 click S "rr:sym/Store"</rr-mermaid>

steps.text: The service stores authenticated uploads immediately. The handler is the centre of this diff: it will join account identity, the bucket and the HTTP response.
Authentication supplies an account and its plan. The new allowance belongs to that account, so its users share one bucket.

Take refills the account’s bucket before it spends: the tokens grow with the seconds since the last call, times the plan’s rate, and stop at the plan’s burst.

A new account starts full; after its first burst, uploads pass at the plan’s steady rate: one a second on Free, five on Pro.

When less than one token is left, Take refuses and returns the wait until the next token. The handler turns that into a Retry-After header in whole seconds.

A plan without a rate is never limited: UploadsPerSec <= 0 returns true before any bucket is made.

Worth checking: rates below one a second, and what a clock that moves backwards does to elapsed.
Free allows one upload per second with a burst of two; Pro allows five with a burst of ten. The renamed configuration also lists Team. The loader decodes these settings.

chapters.title: The handler joins the contract
chapters.lead:
<rr-mermaid>flowchart TD
 P[Plan lookup] --> T[Take]
 T --> H[Handler]
 click P "rr:code/config/limits.json"
 click T "rr:sym/Take"
 click H "rr:sym/ServeHTTP"</rr-mermaid>

steps.text: The handler asks Take before storing a body. A rejected request receives 429 and a Retry-After value rounded up to whole seconds.
The client retries a 429 with the same payload. The handler supplies Retry-After, but the loop never waits; together these paths decide whether a rejected upload can recover.
Two smaller edits ride along on the server: the plans’ rates and the disk store’s path.
And two more where the limit shows: the error’s message and the client’s retry.

chapters.title: Archives and video join the upload allow-list; the rest of the generated type table is unchanged

steps.text: Uploads also accept archives and video now: one block of 23 types in the middle of the generated table.
The table is generated, so the new block should come from the generator's registry rather than a hand edit.

chapters.title: Uploads land in a folder per id prefix

steps.text: The disk store built each file's path by hand, six lines of separators. filepath.Join now does it in one, so the root may end with a slash or not.
The body is capped at a gigabyte while it is written, and a failed close now fails the upload instead of being dropped by defer.
High: Team uploads bypass the limit.
